audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers marked Level 1, Level 6 and First item as Gwen-favoured while their own prose describes an even level 1 and an Aatrox-favoured 6 and first-item window.
audit.why: Aatrox's World Ender (120/100/80s) adds AD, healing and move speed, and his Eclipse/Profane Hydra spike lands before Nashor's-into-Riftmaker; Gwen only flips the lane at two items.
audit.corrected: Skill / Skill / Aatrox / Aatrox / Aatrox / Aatrox / Gwen.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spike text named no cooldowns and mis-titled the passive.
audit.why: World Ender is 120/100/80 and Umbral Dash 9/8/7/6/5 — those numbers make 'wait for it' advice actionable. The passive is A Thousand Cuts, not Thousand Cuts.
audit.corrected: Real cooldowns added to whys[3] and whys[4]; passive name fixed in spikes[3].text and late.

audit.whatIsWrong: Aatrox's Deathbringer Stance auto-attack reset — which also heals him — was never mentioned, and Umbral Dash's in-combo heal was absent.
audit.why: Deathbringer Stance (P) carries autoReset and heal flags; Umbral Dash (E) carries dash and heal on a 9s rank-1 cooldown. The reset wind-up, not the ability cast, is the tell that a knockup is about to be cashed in.
audit.corrected: early and wants.foe[0] now name Deathbringer Stance as the auto reset that converts his knockup into a heal; whys[3] names Umbral Dash's 9s heal.

audit.whatIsWrong: Anti-heal was only mentioned in the late-game paragraph.
audit.why: Aatrox heals from Deathbringer Stance, Umbral Dash and World Ender; Grievous Wounds matters from his first-item spike, not at two items.
audit.corrected: whys[5] now calls for Executioner's Calling at his Eclipse/Hydra spike.

edits.before: Needles ramp the longer the fight goes — extended brawls are yours. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Aatrox's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: World Ender turns his sweetspot chain into an all-in — AD, healing and move speed for the window. Hold Hallowed Mist for the commit, not for poke.

edits.before: Riftmaker is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on World Ender's cooldown.
edits.after: His Eclipse/Profane Hydra lands first — buy Executioner's Calling and farm until Riftmaker.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are your worst window — you are a melee with no untargetability button while he chains knockups and out-trades you every time.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are his window — Umbral Dash heals him mid-combo on a 9s rank-1 cooldown, so his chained knockups out-trade you even with Mist up.

edits.before: His R adds AD, healing and move speed, so his all-in out-sustains your Snip Snip! poke unless you time the Mist on his commit perfectly.
edits.after: World Ender's 120s rank-1 cooldown buys him AD, healing and move speed, so his all-in out-sustains your poke unless Mist lands on the commit.

edits.before: His Eclipse/Profane Hydra spike lands before your Nashor's-into-Riftmaker, so his drain out-grinds you in extended fights — survive, do not duel.
edits.after: His Eclipse/Profane Hydra spike lands before your Nashor's-into-Riftmaker — buy Executioner's Calling early so his drain stops out-grinding you.

edits.before: Riftmaker omnivamp/true-damage plus Thousand Cuts %-max-HP magic chews through the bruiser HP he stacks faster than his R-window heal can refund it — this is where you flip the lane.
edits.after: Riftmaker omnivamp/true damage plus A Thousand Cuts %-max-HP magic chews through the bruiser HP he stacks faster than his R-window heal can refund it — this is where you flip the lane.

edits.before: Land the full Q1-Q2-Q3 sweetspot chain to knock you up repeatedly and stat-check you before you can drop Mist
edits.after: Chain Q1-Q2-Q3 sweetspots into a Deathbringer Stance auto reset — that empowered swing heals him and stat-checks you

edits.before: Levels 1-3 are a coin flip — Aatrox is just as weak early as you are, with a slow, dodgeable first Q sweetspot and no real burst until he chains all three casts. Last-hit at the tip of your Snip Snip! cone and DO NOT walk up for a Q he can punish with a sweetspot knockup into a free auto. Respect his W (Infernal Chains): if the ring lands and you stay inside it he yanks you back toward his sword zone, so step out of the circle before it detonates. Neither of you wins a clean all-in yet, so trade Q tips, dodge his sweetspots, and farm.
edits.after: Levels 1-3 are a coin flip — Aatrox is just as weak early as you are, with a slow, dodgeable first Q sweetspot and no real burst until he chains all three casts. Last-hit at the cone tip and never walk up for a Q he can punish: the sweetspot knockup feeds his Deathbringer Stance auto reset, which heals him. Respect his W (Infernal Chains, 20s at rank 1): if the ring lands and you stay inside it he yanks you back toward his sword zone, so step out of the circle before it detonates. Neither of you wins a clean all-in yet, so trade Q tips, dodge his sweetspots, and farm.

edits.before: At two-plus items you take the lane back. Aatrox is a drain-bruiser who stacks HP, and that is exactly what your passive Thousand Cuts and percent-max-HP Snip Snip! were built to punish — the bigger his bar, the harder your magic Q lands and the more your abilities heal you. With Nashor's into Riftmaker online and Mist for the all-in, you out-grind him because his R-window healing and Hydra drain can't keep pace with %-max-HP plus your true-damage center snip and Riftmaker conversion. Anti-heal (Morellonomicon) seals it: cut his sustain and the extended trade he wanted becomes the trade you win.
edits.after: At two-plus items you take the lane back. notes: Level chart disagreed across layers: content win[] and full phases[].side both said Gwen wins Level 1, Level 6 and First item, while the prose in whys[0], whys[4] and whys[5] says the opposite (skill at 1, Aatrox at 6 and at his Eclipse/Hydra spike). Aligned both layers to the prose. Suspect names 'Snip Snip' and 'Thousand Cuts' are near-misses: 'Snip Snip!' was already correct in the text (false positive); 'Thousand Cuts' was genuinely missing its 'A' and is fixed. The full layer for Gwen is heavily templated (same sentences reused across matchups) — phases[].why and breakdown.* read generic almost everywhere, not just here. Aatrox's W is flagged 'grounding' in the kit; Riot's description only says pull/slow, so I did not assert grounding.
